assessment: This paper uses an innovative cell-free protein-protein interaction system to identify factors that interact with HSV-1 capsids in infected cells. In addition to cataloging numerous capsid-interacting proteins, the manuscript probes the antiviral mechanism of one of these, MxB. The data provide strong support for an intriguing model in which MxB "punches" holes in HSV-1 capsids, releasing viral DNA and potentially triggering host DNA sensors. Moreover, the results suggest that viral proteins bind to and shield the capsids from MxB attack, offering a new perspective on how viruses might evade some host defenses.
